title: Bus accident near Truth or Consequences and the lawsuit
summary: Tire blowout, pinned in bus, Chuck Beatty rescued him; settlement funded his record company.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Mm-hmm. Yeah, I also see where, after you left, looks like June Gardner joined the band.
Yeah, he joined them to go to Europe with Hampton. Mm-hmm. Because I couldn't go because of the accident I was in.
Yeah, I see this in the Louisiana Weekly. Yeah, there's a notice here in the Weekly that you were in some kind of accident. What happened? Yeah.

What happened? The bus was going, we were going from El Paso to Albuquerque, New Mexico, and we got to a place to call it Truth of Consequence, Mexico. Mm-hmm. The bus was going about 80 or 90 miles an hour, and the front tire blew out. And we went down a 15-foot embankment. All right. And I was pinned down in the bus, and everybody got out the bus except me and the bus driver. And Chuck Beatty was the one who got me out. And how he got me out, he was trying to pull that seat up off me, because I was pinned down by the feet, by the legs, and I mean, so, Chuck said, there's a lot of cars around there, trucks around there, trying to help out, get the fellas off the bus and everything. But I was, they couldn't get me out, and the bus started smoking. I thought, sure, that bus was going to catch a fire. So, they tied a chain, a big chain around my next seat, and tied the other part to a truck. Right. And, but the chain popped, and they still couldn't get me out. So Chuck asked, one of the drivers in the car, did he have an automobile jacked? And he jacked that thing off my leg. I didn't know I was waiting until I got ready to get up. I said, I can't move. They had to take me off the bus, carry me off.
Did you have to go to the hospital?

Oh, yeah. The doctors told me I wouldn't walk anymore. But I started walking with crutches, and they told me I'd have to walk with crutches the rest of my life. So, then they put me on a cane. I walked with a cane for a few years. And then I put the cane down and started walking. And just this year, it started giving me trouble again.
So this was, so you got some compensation from, from Lionel Hampton's band?
No, no, from Firestone Tie Company. Oh, okay.
So there was a lawsuit. Yeah.

A lawsuit. Yeah, because the tie blew out. And it was a defect in the tie. But I don't think there was a defect in the tie. But I'm glad they did say that. See we played Las Vegas, and they had Las Vegas every day. It was about 105. And we stayed there a month. And that bus stayed in the hot sun outside at that time. And when we, when we left Las Vegas, we went to El Paso. Then from El Paso, we were coming back to New Mexico. And we got about 50 miles from New Mexico. That's when the tie blew out. And it went down this embankment. Right. The bus looked like a U. I don't see how anybody survived that crash.

So you got 27,000 from the lawsuit. Yeah. Was this some of the money you used to finance a record company? Yeah. Oh, okay. Well, that explains where you got the money for the record company. When, when, what years were you living in New York? I think you said for some time, for a period.
Oh, I lived in New York. Before I moved my family to New York, let me see. I went to the state about 10 years in New York.

Yeah. See, now, when I came back here, I wasn't in, no, I didn't come back here to stay. Lionel Hampton, they had just built a Royal Finestas, and Lionel, hey, why was going to come back to the band, say, we're getting ready to go to New Orleans.
